name: Workflow - Payment to Personalized Welcome Email (PayPal webhook simulation, OpenAI, Supabase)

nodes.name: Payment Webhook (simulated PayPal IPN - point at real webhook later)
nodes.notes: Trigger node. Derek will manually point this at a real PayPal webhook later (or swap for a Webhook node if n8n requires a listener instead of an outbound HTTP Request — left as HTTP Request per the build spec). Expected incoming JSON shape: { payer_name, payer_email, company, tier, amount_paid, currency, paypal_txn_id }.

values.content: You write a short, warm, personalized welcome email body for a new paying customer of an empire company. Use the per-company prompt from openai-prompts.json (automation/openai-prompts.json) — look up the entry matching the {{ $json.company }} slug and follow its system_prompt for tone, services, and pricing facts; never invent pricing or services not listed there. Output HTML body content only (no <html>/<head> wrapper, no subject line). Keep it under 150 words. Never disclose internal AI tooling or say 'I am an AI' in a way that conflicts with the per-company brand rules (OmniGuard/Kiaros-adjacent brands must never reveal AI branding to end users at all).
Write the welcome email body for: payer_name={{ $json.payer_name }}, company={{ $json.company }}, tier={{ $json.tier }}, amount_paid={{ $json.amount_paid }} {{ $json.currency }}.

nodes.name: Insert Payment (Supabase)
nodes.notes: Inserts into the `payments` table (see automation/supabase-tables.sql). payments.user_id is a FK to users(id) — this node does not set it because matching the payer to an existing `users` row is a separate lookup not scoped here; add a Supabase 'get' node before this one (filter users by email) and map its id into user_id if you want payments linked to users automatically.
